news.title: Atlas Robot’s New Hand May Outperform Humanlike Designs
paras: Robots need a hand that can pick, move, and grip objects easily to help them work in real life. Building such a hand is very hard because it must be strong, flexible, and simple to make. Boston Dynamics says their new robot hand should have three fingers and one thumb.

The hand needs 13 degrees of freedom, meaning 13 movable joints. These joints let the robot grasp objects in many ways, just like a human hand. Because of this design, the robot can pick delicate items without crushing them, making it safer for people.

news.title: Intel gets waiver after worries fuzzy US ban on foreign-made robots may hit fabs
paras: 21 The interior of Intel's chip manufacturing facility named Fab 52 in Chandler, Arizona. The uncertainty surrounding the Federal Communications Commission ban on certain foreign-made robots was revealed in the agency’s decision to grant Intel’s waiver request.

On October 22, the FCC published its order allowing Intel to continue using the foreign-made robots in US semiconductor manufacturing facilities for a period of one year. The robots in question are automated guided vehicles operating on “tracks or predefined paths” while often requiring operator oversight, according to Intel’s website. They help to move materials and items around within warehouses and factory floors.

news.title: 'Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' was afraid to say anything in season of gimmicks
paras: The entire season was one giant gimmick, and that gimmick was shoving "Trek" into as many genres as possible and often directly adapting classic films from those genres. You could argue that an entire season of gimmick episodes is a bold risk: putting the characters in fun, wacky situations to see how they react.

It could be interesting, but the season we got never made the most of the concept. It was all so safe and paint-by-numbers, and, most importantly, it didn't have anything profound or interesting to say. "Star Trek" — a show built on progressive ideals, thoughtful characters, and boundary-breaking television — was completely and totally afraid to say anything at all.

news.title: Is Taekwondo an art or A Sport?
paras: And then… silence, and then someone from the crowd shouted… “Is Taekwondo a sport or is it a performing arts?” Well we are here to answer that question! Did you know that Taekwondo is Korean? In Korean, chung and hung mean blue and red.

They use these colours to represent a competitor at a competition. You wear protective gear in that colour on your stomach. Otherwise, you wear your own white gear. According to sources such as The Korea Herald and Kiddle, Taekwondo is a form of performing art, because you don’t just fight, you learn a pattern.

news.title: Zoo animals enjoy spooktacular Halloween treats
paras: Animals at Whipsnade Zoo are enjoying an early taste of Halloween with some special treats. The lemurs and macaques tucked into carved pumpkins to find sweetcorn and peppers, whilst rhino Hugo enjoyed his usual breakfast of hay and cabbage.

The zoo's keepers been trying to find creative ways to encourage the animals' natural instincts to hunt and explore. Matthew Webb, Head of Zoological Operations at Whipsnade Zoo, said: "As everyone counts down to Halloween, our zookeepers used seasonal squashes to make sure the animals don't miss out on any of the fun"

sport.title: ‘Staying healthy is a real skill’: Mouratoglou explains why Zverev deserves to be No. 1
paras: Patrick Mouratoglou believes Alexander Zverev fully deserves his No. 1 ranking, even if Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz are better players.

Staying healthy, he argues, is “a real skill” that demands sacrifice, and Zverev’s two Grand Slam titles in 2026 marked a mental breakthrough. Alexander Zverev may not be the best player in the world, but his ranking is fully deserved. That is Patrick Mouratoglou’s view, set out in a video on his social media channels in which he argued that staying healthy is a skill in itself, and part of a player’s value.

sport.title: Elena Rybakina Reaches First Tour Final As World No.1 In Ningbo
paras: Elena Rybakina continued her title defence at the Ningbo Open with a tricky win over Diana Shnaider in the semi-finals on Saturday. The world No.1 had to overcome blips in both sets during her 6-3, 7-5 win over the Russian sixth seed.

Rybakina now leads Shnaider 3-0 in their head-to-head and has recorded 52 Tour-level wins this season, which is more than any other player. She is through to her sixth final of the season. “She played really well and it’s always difficult to play against lefties, we don’t have so many on the Tour,” Rybakina said afterwards.

sport.title: October 24, 1999: The day Amelie Mauresmo claimed her first WTA singles title
paras: On this day in tennis history, two young budding superstars faced off and it was Mauresmo who won her maiden crown On this day, October 24, 1999, a 20-year-old Amelie Mauresmo claimed her maiden title in Bratislava, defeating another rising star in 16-year-old Kim Clijsters (6-3, 6-3).

It was the first of 15 clashes between two future world No 1s, and, for the French player, the first of the 25 singles titles that she would win throughout her career. She was successful at a young age, winning in the juniors rank at both Roland-Garros and Wimbledon in 1996.

sport.title: Arthur Fils claims he’s done something this year that ‘rarely happens’ as he closes in on ATP Finals qualifica
paras: Arthur Fils has enjoyed an extraordinary year, and it feels like vindication after the fitness turmoil he’s been forced to deal with thus far in his young career. A persistent back injury that started last year halted his rapid progression and saw him miss the bulk of 2025.

It was this huge setback, and therefore how far he has come from that devastation, which made his maiden Masters 1000 title in Cincinnati that much sweeter. And, the Frenchman is due to get another deserved reward for all his hard work throughout this campaign, as he closes in on ATP Finals qualification.

sport.title: Carlos Alcaraz to play US Open semi-finalist in the first round of the Vienna Open as nightmare draw is confir
paras: Carlos Alcaraz will return to the Vienna Open for the first time in five years next week, in a bid to regain his full fitness and increase his indoor preparation. Historically, the Spaniard has struggled at this latter stage of the season, with the Shanghai and Paris Masters having both eluded him thus far in his career.

He will hope to right those wrongs in the French capital next month, and a strong showing in the Austrian capital will certainly help his cause. After all, Carlos Alcaraz ’s draw for the Vienna Open has now been revealed, and it’s not been kind.
